before.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: virus natural history.
choices: HBV is a partially double-stranded DNA virus that persists through covalently closed circular DNA and can cause acute infection, chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
Calling one normal ALT value proof of inactive disease can miss dynamic infection.
Use one isolated laboratory value without reviewing the full serology pattern, fibrosis, treatment history, or current guidance.
Assume viral suppression removes every need for monitoring, vaccination, or cancer surveillance.
before.rationale: HBV is a partially double-stranded DNA virus that persists through covalently closed circular DNA and can cause acute infection, chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Use age at acquisition, immune status, ALT, HBV DNA, HBeAg, fibrosis, and comorbidity to interpret disease trajectory.

after.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: virus natural history.
choices: HBV is a partially double-stranded DNA virus with a persistent nuclear cccDNA reservoir
HBV has an RNA-only genome and never forms a DNA intermediate
HBV persists primarily in red blood cells rather than hepatocytes
Undetectable serum HBV DNA proves that nuclear cccDNA has been eliminated
after.rationale: HBV carries partially double-stranded DNA and forms cccDNA in hepatocytes. Polymerase-directed treatment can suppress circulating DNA without reliably removing the reservoir; suppression is not proof of eradication.
